data.title: Netflix Stock: Streaming Giant Buys Historic Seinfeld Lot | Investor's Business Daily
data.summary: The tech sector kept on consuming Hollywood and TV land on Tuesday, after it became clear that nobody else would bid on the historic site where Seinfeld episodes and John Wayne Westerns were filmed. With apparently no other takers after a foreclosure auction by Goldman Sachs (GS), Netflix (NFLX) swooped in to buy the nearly century-old Radford Studio Center. data.title: Here's What Would Prove Me Wrong About Netflix Stock
data.summary: Advertising was supposed to become Netflix's other big growth engine, and it's taking longer than planned. Ad revenue climbed more than 150% in 2025, to over $1.5 billion, and in January, management expected it to roughly double this year. In October, Netflix said it now expects around $2.7 billion instead, because some of its ad features have rolled out a bit more slowly than planned. [...] Even $2.7 billion would be fast growth, just slower than 2025's rate and the original plan. And Netflix plans to launch its ad-supported tier in 15 more countries in 2027, starting with 12 of them in March. My bar is the $3 billion Netflix first expected for this year. If 2027 ad revenue can't top that level, even with another year plus 15 new countries, I'd see the issue as more than a slow rollout. The margin matters most [...] Much of the streaming service's growth comes from hiking prices, which usually works only while members keep watching. They still are. In the first half of 2026, members watched more than 97 billion hours on Netflix, up 2% year over year and a bit faster than the 1.5% gain in all of 2025. Members also took this year's price hikes much as they took past ones, management said in October.

data.title: Deepening Our Commitment to Los Angeles: Netflix Purchases Radford Studio Center - About Netflix
data.summary: Today, we’re proud to share that Netflix is purchasing Radford to build on that history and strengthen our investment in Los Angeles and California. [...] Business 24 November 2026 Unless you work in entertainment or live in Los Angeles, you may not have heard of Radford Studio Center. But you’ve probably seen something that was made there. Opened in 1928, at the end of the silent film era, Radford has been home to a long list of classic shows — from Gunsmoke and Gilligan's Island to The Mary Tyler Moore Show, Seinfeld, and That ‘70s Show, among many, many others. [...] There’s still a long way to go, but we are hopeful that with the partnership of the State of California and the City of Los Angeles, this will be the start of a meaningful new investment in California's film industry. This city is home to us. We’re excited to keep investing here and finding more ways to entertain the world, while supporting the writers, builders, electricians, drivers, designers, and talent who make LA, California, and the entertainment industry so special.

data.title: Beloved drive-thru worker and star of Netflix film "on top of the world" after making a year's salary on last day of work - CBS News
data.summary: That short film, called "One Last Order," premieres on Netflix Tuesday and has already garnered awards from the Aspen Shortfest, Nantucket Film Festival, Miami Film Festival and more. The movie documents Williams' final day on the job, but it also shows the side of Williams that her beloved customers didn't see, like how she raised five girls — her sister and niece's children — as her own. The film shares how she lived in a house for a while with no running water or electricity. [...] Beloved drive-thru worker and star of Netflix film "on top of the world" after making a year's salary on last day of work Sighle Williams keeps it simple. "I just like to treat people the way I like to be treated," she told "CBS Mornings." So when Williams, who'd spent her 37-year career making people smile at Mac's Drive Thru in Gainesville, Florida, was approached about having a documentary made about her last day, she was excited but a bit skeptical. [...] The whole thing made her feel on "top of the world," she told "CBS Mornings." "I didn't even eat all day, I didn't go to the restroom all day," Williams said, "I was just so -- I wanted to acknowledge everybody and thank everybody for coming out, you know, sharing the love with me on my last day." She ended up making a year's salary on that final day, but won't reveal how much she made. "I don't want nobody to feel no type of way because, you know, I'm hamburgers and fries," she said.
